mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,000K units signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1.0% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during such periods of sustained industrial production decline.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth above 250K per month for two consecutive months, combined with a rising unemployment rate, signals a labor market imbalance that can precede cyclical corrections and result in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 250000 AND UNRATE rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during such labor market imbalance episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Consumer Price Index above 3% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which typically precedes central bank tightening and higher interest rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained CPIAUCSL above 3% for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both the federal funds rate and the 10-year Treasury yield (not available, so use RSAFS as a proxy for savings/investment rate) below historical averages signals a loosening of financial conditions, which boosts equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and RSAFS both below 5-year moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when both FEDFUNDS and RSAFS are below their 5-year averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by GDPC1 growth) above 0.5% for four consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in consumer spending (INDPRO flat), signals a savings glut that depresses near-term corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change > 0.5% for 4 consecutive months AND INDPRO monthly change ≈ 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during such episodes of rising income with flat industrial production.
